violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 41F, No More than 6 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours. Chicken soup cooked yesterday and placed in the walk-in to cool was 50º during today’s inspection. Another container was 47º.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. Both containers of soup were discarded.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Sanitizers, Criteria
violations.observation: The concentration of the quaternary ammonia solution was measured over 500 ppm. This concentration exceeds the approved limits for use with food-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils in a foodservice establishment.
violations.corrective_action: Maintain the concentration of 150 and 400 ppm. Verify concentration using the appropriate test kit. This was corrected during the inspection.

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Equipment/Utensils, No Cloth Drying
violations.observation: After being run through the warewashing machine, equipment and utensils were observed being cloth-dried rather than air-dried after cleaning and chemical sanitization.
violations.corrective_action: After cleaning and sanitizing, equipment and utensils may not be cloth dried. Discontinue cloth drying utensils and equipment. Correct as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months. CELEBRITY DELLY (Inspection Date: 09/15/2026) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Handled Single-Service/Use Items Storage
violations.observation: Unwrapped knives, forks, or spoons were not stored with the handles up. Metal utensils and plastic utensils were not stored properly. They were stored with handles not lined or with eating portions up in the holder.
violations.corrective_action: Knives, forks, and spoons that are not prewrapped shall be presented so that only the handles are touched by employees and consumers if consumer self- service is provided. The food employees corrected this by rearranging the utensils during the inspection.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following equipment is not operating properly and/or is in poor repair: the mixing station for the quaternary ammonia solution was not working properly and was not dispensing quaternary ammonia at the correct concentration. Food employees were manually mixing the solutions and they were too high.
violations.corrective_action: Equipment shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. Repair the quaternary ammonia dispensing station as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months.

violations.title: Plumbing System, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: Plumbing connections under the hand sink in the kitchen are leaking.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair. Repair as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months.

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 41F, No More than 6 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours. Several foods in the walk-in cooked yesterday or earlier had not been cooled properly in the walk-in refrigerator. Chicken noodle soup made yesterday was 46º (2 containers); whole roast beef cooked yesterday was 53º; cooked ham cooked 3/12 was 46º; and shredded chicken cooked today at 9:00 am was 46º.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. All foods were discarded except for the shredded chicken which was placed in a shallow pan and moved to the freezer to cool. CDI.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: egg salad was 46º in the walk-in. Sliced tomatoes sliced yesterday were 46º. Sliced cheese in the front counter refrigerator was 48º. Tuna salad in the 3-door table top refrigerator was 47º.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. The cheese and tuna salad were moved to another unit. The sliced tomatoes were discarded. CDI.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: large roasts, large containers of soup, large containers of egg salad and sliced tomatoes were not cooling properly. These foods were placed in the walk-in in large covered plastic containers, which will not facilitate proper cooling.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. The establishment has cooling wands, shallow pans and a walk-in freezer. All should be used to make food cool faster. The EHS discussed this with the owner and PIC.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Miscellaneous Source Contamination
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were found subject to contamination after receipt and during storage due to the condition as described: an open bin of ice and an open pitcher of water for ice water was stored directly next to the only hand washing sink behind the front counter with the soap dispenser located directly behind the ice and water, exposing it to contamination.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 through 3-306. The PIC temporarily installed a cutting board to separate the ice/water from the handsink, but now it’s difficult to access the handsoap. Please come up with a permanent solution which may be moving the ice and water containers.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following refrigeration unit is not operating properly and is unable to maintain cold food at or below 41F: There are three units which need service: the knish unit, the unit for cheeses and dressings at the front counter and the walk-in. The ambient temperature of the knish holding unit was 45º. Most foods in the walk-in were 46º. The ambient temperature of the cheese and dressings unit was 50º.
violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly. Please have both units serviced to ensure they are working properly and repaired if not. Notify your EHS when they have been repaired.

violations.title: Equipment Clean to Sight and Touch
violations.observation: Encrusted grease deposits and/or other soil deposits were observed on the food contact surfaces of the following cooking equipment: the internal parts of the French fry cutter over the 3-compartment sink was visibly soiled and in need of cleaning.
violations.corrective_action: The food-contact surfaces of cooking equipment and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. A surface that is soiled cannot be effectively sanitized.

violations.title: Plumbing System, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: Plumbing connections under the hand sink in the kitchen were leaking and the waste was being collected in a five gallon bucket.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair. Repair the leak as soon as possible and before the follow-up in 10 days.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: Observed that the drop ceiling in the kitchen is not maintained in good repair. Several panels were missing, damaged, or stained. Also, the ceiling panels installed are the wrong type. Ceiling panels must be smooth and easily cleanable (restaurant grade). The current ones are office or home-standard type.
violations.corrective_action: Replace the missing, damaged and stained ceiling panels with restaurant grade ones. Come up with a plan to replace the remaining unapproved panels. Correct as soon as possible or within 90 days.

violations.title: Food Protection Manager - Accredited Program
violations.observation: There was no certified food manager present when the inspection began.
violations.corrective_action: The CFM arrived during the inspection. It is recommended that more food employees obtain food manager certification.

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. At the time of this inspection, the Health Department provided and reviewed handouts and resource information in a red folder labeled 'Employee Health Policy.'
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. The EHS provided the manager with the model FCHD policy. Before the next inspection, have all food employees read and sign the forms.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. The EHS provided the manager with a copy of the FCHD model policy.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Water Temp
violations.observation: The handwashing sink on prep line is equipped with separate cold and hot water faucets rather than a mixing valve or combination faucet and there was no hot water provided. The faucet handle had broken off and needs to be replaced.
violations.corrective_action: A handwashing sink shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 100F through a mixing valve or combination faucet. The manager stated the faucet handle is in the process of being replaced. Correct by Friday September 19.

violations.title: Handwashing Signage
violations.observation: Observed that sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands is not provided or is not clearly visible at all handwashing sinks used by food employees. The required sign was missing in the kitchen handsink.
violations.corrective_action: Provide a visible sign or poster at all handwashing sinks used by food employees that reminds food employees to wash their hands. Correct as soon as possible or before the next inspection.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: raw shell eggs were stored over ready to eat foods in the Max Cold unit.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. The manager moved the eggs to correct this. CELEBRITY DELLY (Inspection Date: 09/09/2025) Page 2 of 4

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 41F, No More than 6 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours. Corned beef cooked yesterday and placed in the walk-in was 44 degrees F during today’s inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. The manager discarded the corned beef.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: several foods in the prep units were out of cold holding temperature to include: cooked salmon at 85F, packaged cold cuts 62F, cooked packaged chicken 50F, Cole slaw 54F, sliced tomatoes 52F, individually portioned cooked corned beef for sandwiches 46F, individually portioned cooked pastrami for sandwiches 49F, and tuna salad 48F. Foods were in this unit for less than 4 hours.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. The manager stated there foods were out of temperature due to the prep top containers being uncovered during the rush. That is possible, however commercial refrigeration units are designed to keep foods cold even during rush periods. The EHS observed that foods containers were stacked high in the prep top units and that cold cuts were individually wrapped in plastic. Both conditions will prevent cold air from getting to foods and keeping it cold in storage. The manager agreed to rapidly cool all the foods down in the freezer or discard them if he could not.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Separation of Poison/Toxic Materials
violations.observation: Observed that poisonous and toxic materials are not properly stored to prevent the contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens or single service items. A wiping cloth bucket was stored on the prep counter where the slicer is located.
violations.corrective_action: All poisonous and toxic materials shall be stored to prevent contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items by separating the poisonous and toxic materials by spacing or partitioning. The manager had food employees move the wiping cloth container.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: multiple large pieces of cooked corned beef, turkey, and pastrami were placed stacked in 5-gallon buckets in the walk-in to cool; 5 gallon buckets of reserved cooking liquids from meats were placed in 5-gallon buckets hot. Meats just removed from the oven were placed in sealed, full 4 inch inserts to “cool” according to kitchen staff.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. The cooling methods observed today are not approved and will not allow foods to cool within the permitted time. The EHS explained to the manager the importance of cooling and suggested placing the cooked meats on sheet pans and cooling in the freezer and using cooling wands and the freezer to cooling the reserved cooking liquids. The manager had his food employees place the cooling meats in the freezer, and incorporate cooling wands for the reserved liquids. He also has them uncover and separate the meats just cooked so they would cool properly.

violations.title: Food Thermometer, Repair and Calibration
violations.observation: The food temperature measuring device in the knish unit was found out of calibration in the range of use.
violations.corrective_action: Food thermometers shall be calibrated in accordance with manufacturer's specifications as necessary to ensure their accuracy. It is suggested that food thermometers be calibrated at least once a week in a cup completely filled with ice and cold water to a temperature of 32F or calibrated in a pot of boiling water at 212F. Replace the thermometer in this unit before the next inspection.

violations.title: Jewelry
violations.observation: Employees observed wearing jewelry on their arms and hands while preparing food.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall limit their jewelry to a plain wedding ring while preparing food. Food employees may not wear bracelets, watches, etc. because they can inhibit proper hand washing.

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored on the counter.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses. Correct as soon as possible or before the next inspection.

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Equipment/Utensils, No Cloth Drying
violations.observation: Observed the dishwashing employee cloth-drying all equipment from the warewashing machine rather than air-dried after cleaning and chemical sanitization.
violations.corrective_action: After cleaning and sanitizing, equipment and utensils may not be cloth dried. Correct as soon as possible or within 6 months.

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces Kept Clean
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surfaces of the following equipment had accumulations of grime and debris: the shelving next to the range was visibly soiled.
violations.corrective_action: Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. Correct as soon as possible or before the next inspection.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Mops Allowed to Air Dry
violations.observation: Observed that mops are improperly stored between use.
violations.corrective_action: Store mops in a position that allows them to air dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies. Correct as soon as possible or within six months.

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: Observed several ceiling panels out of place and holes in walls that needs to be repaired to prevent vermin entry.
violations.corrective_action: Repair the physical facilities. Poor repair and maintenance compromises the functionality of the physical facilities.Correct as soon as possible or within six months. CELEBRITY DELLY (Inspection Date: 09/09/2025) Page 3 of 4

out_items.name: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use

violations.title: Eating, Drinking, or Using Tobacco
violations.observation: A food employee was observed drinking in dish pit where they may contaminate food, clean equipment, utensils or other items needing protection.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees may only eat, drink, or use tobacco in a designated area like a dining room or office area. Employees shall not eat or drink in the kitchen areas, warewashing areas, or storage areas where items may become contaminated. PIC trained all staff on proper eating and drinking locations within establishment.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: raw chicken stored above cooked Canadian bacon at 2 dr Avantco prep cooler; raw shell eggs stored above ranch in 2 dr upright display
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. PIC placed all raw animal foods below all ready to eat items.

violations.title: Non-TCS Food Contact Surface, Clean per Manufacturer
violations.observation: Internal surfaces of ice machine are not being cleaned as required.
violations.corrective_action: Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is NOT time/temperature control for safety food such as ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, and enclosed components of equipment such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, beverage and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending equipment at a frequency specified by the manufacturer or at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. PIC properly cleaned internal surfaces of ice machine.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: chilli (125F) in steam well.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. PIC reheated chilli to 165F before placing in steam well.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: potato knish (46F) in 1 DR Danby display cooler; sliced Provolone cheese (50F), sliced Swiss cheese (55F), sliced American cheese (42F), sauerkraut (51F) in ice bath on the top of 2 DR freezer Avantco.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. PIC discarded potato knish and moved all other food items to WIC.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food, Disposition
violations.observation: Observed the following ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food being held for more than the specified time/temperature allowed: Sliced provolone cheese (2/12) in 2 DR UC Avantco, pickled onions (2/1) in 2 DR upright display.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be discarded if it: 1) exceeds 7 days or at 41F (except the time it is frozen); or 2) is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day. PIC discarded provolone cheese & pickled onions. CELEBRITY DELLY (Inspection Date: 02/19/2025) Page 2 of 4

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: raw ground beef in 3-compartment sink under running water at 78F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. PIC placed raw ground beef under running water below 70F.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. Observed bread in plastic bag stored on the floor of WIC; Puff pastry dough in boxes observed on the freezer floor.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. PIC placed aforementioned food items on storage racks.

violations.title: Miscellaneous Source Contamination
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were found subject to contamination after receipt and during storage due to the condition as described: observed flour in bulk dry storage bin contaminated with beef blood.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 through 3-306. PIC discarded flour and cleaned and sanitized the working bin.
